raw_text:
Here’s a clean, integrated 12-week plan from scratch: strength, cardio (upscaled weeks 4–8, peak 9–12), recovery/mobility, and nutrition. All lower-body work stays low-impact with controlled ROM; no jumping or deep knee flexion under load. Goal: restore strength/control and feel strong by Week 12 for return to skiing.

Global structure
- Weekly schedule template
  - Mon: Strength A (Lower focus) + cooldown
  - Tue: Cardio Session 1 + micro-mobility
  - Wed: Strength B (Upper + posterior chain) + micro-mobility
  - Thu: Recovery Session A (20–30 min mobility/stability) or Rest
  - Fri: Strength C (Lower hip hinge + unilateral) + cooldown
  - Sat: Cardio Session 2 + Recovery Session B (20–30 min)
  - Sun: Rest or easy walk + micro-mobility
- Warm-up every session (10–12 min): 5–6 min easy bike; ankle rocks; hip flexor stretch; thoracic rotations; activation (mini-band lateral walks, clamshells, glute bridge isos, TKEs).
- Pain/ROM rules: Work in symptom-free ranges; avoid loaded deep flexion (>~60–70° initially). Pain >3/10 or swelling >24 h → reduce ROM, load, or swap to hip-dominant work.

Strength training (3 days/week; RIR 1–3; rest 90–150 s on primaries)
Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): Foundation and tolerance
- Week 1
  - Day A: Leg press partial 3×12; Spanish squat iso 3×20–30 s; High-box squat 4×6 light; DB RDL 3×10; standing calf 3×12–15; Pallof press 3×10/side.
  - Day B: Bench 4×6–8; chest-supported row 4×8–10; half-kneel landmine press 3×8/side; lat pulldown 3×10; rear delt fly 3×12–15; 45° back extension 3×10.
  - Day C: Trap bar DL (high handles) 4×5; reverse lunge to box 3×6/leg light; seated ham curl 3×10–12; low step-up 3×6/leg; side plank 3×20–30 s/side.
- Week 2: +2.5–5% load if pain-free; keep ROM; add TKEs 2×15 on Days A/C; Spanish squat iso 3×30–40 s.
- Week 3: Add 1 set to leg press and trap bar; introduce assisted split squat to pads 3×8/side (shallow); balance: single-leg stance on foam 3×30 s/side (Day A finisher).

Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6): Strength accumulation
- Week 4
  - Day A: Leg press 4×8–10; Box squat 5×4; Spanish squat iso 3×30–45 s; Split squat to pads 3×6/side; calf 4×10–12; Pallof half-kneel 3×10/side.
  - Day B: Incline DB press 4×6–8; 1-arm cable row 4×8/side; landmine press 3×8/side; face pull 3×12–15; prone ham curl 3×8–10 (slow ecc); supported hip airplanes 3×4/side.
  - Day C: Trap bar DL 5×3; RDL 3×6–8; step-up 8–10 in 4×5/leg; Copenhagen plank (short lever) 3×15–20 s; suitcase carry 3×30–40 m/side.

  - Session B: Cat–camel; thread-the-needle; thoracic extension on roller; dead bugs; side planks; Pallof isos 2×20–30 s; wall sits 2×30–60 s at pain-free angle.
- Flare playbook: Reduce ROM 20–30%, swap knee-dominant work for hinges/isometrics, use compression/elevation; ice only if symptomatic; resume progress once next-day reactivity resolves.

- Daily targets
  - Calories: Start BW(kg) × 30–33 kcal; adjust ±100–150 kcal if weekly average weight shifts >0.25%.
  - Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day, spread over 3–5 meals (25–40 g/meal).
  - Carbs: 3–4.5 g/kg/day; bias toward pre/post training.
  - Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day. Fiber 25–40 g/day. Hydration 30–40 ml/kg/day (+500–750 ml around training).

  - Rest days: keep protein; slightly reduce carbs (remove pre/post boluses).
- Food quality: lean proteins, dairy/eggs, fish 2–3×/wk; rice/potatoes/oats/fruit; olive oil/avocado/nuts; plenty of veg; vitamin C, calcium, vitamin D sources.
- Supplements (optional): Creatine 3–5 g/day; collagen/gelatin 10–15 g + 50–100 mg vitamin C 30–60 min pre-lower-body if tendon discomfort; omega-3 1–2 g EPA/DHA/day if low fish; whey/plant protein; magnesium glycinate 200–400 mg at night if needed.
- Tracking: Weigh 3–4 mornings/week; adjust intake to keep weight stable and performance high.

Return-to-ski readiness checks by Week 12
- Pain-free completion of sessions; no next-day swelling.
- Box squat and leg press strong in controlled ROM; trap bar singles at RPE 7–8 move crisply.
- Step-up to 10–12 in with control, no valgus; 60 s wall sit pain-free at training angle.
- Balance: 30 s single-leg with head turns/perturbations.
- Subjective confidence ≥8/10 on stairs, hills, and lateral moves.

Coach notes
- Progress one variable at a time (load, ROM, or density). Log box/step heights to progress safely.
- Keep cadence high/moderate resistance on cardio to avoid deep flexion.
- If knee reactivity appears, pull back cardio volume first, then lower-body ROM; keep upper body and hinge patterns rolling.

Below is a 12‑week, low‑impact strength program designed for a 36-year-old recreational lifter post right medial meniscus tear (6 months post-op/rehab, cleared for low-impact strength; no jumping, no deep knee flexion under load). Goal: restore lower-body strength and control for return to skiing while building whole-body strength and resiliency. The plan emphasizes controlled ROM within pain-free ranges, progressive loading, tempo control, isometrics, and unilateral balance/hip strategy important for skiing. Includes week-by-week structure, session details, and recovery guidance.

Global guidelines
- Frequency: 3 strength days/week (A, B, C), 1 optional accessory/conditioning day.
- Effort/tempo: Controlled 3–0–3 to 2–0–2 tempos on key knee-dominant moves, strict technique, no valgus collapse. Stop sets 1–2 reps before technical failure. Pain >3/10 or swelling that lasts >24 h = regress or skip that pattern.
- ROM: Avoid deep knee flexion under load. Use box/bench heights to cap squat/lunge depth around 45–60° knee flexion initially; progress only if symptom-free.
- Unilateral balance: Prioritize hip-dominant patterns and deceleration control; build frontal/transverse plane stability.
- Cardio: 2–3 low-impact sessions/week (bike, elliptical, rowing, sled push/pull) 20–35 min Z2. No running/jumping.
- Warm-up every session (10–12 min): 
  1) Tissue/activation: foam roll quads, adductors, lateral glute, calf (30–45 s each); 
  2) Mobility: ankle dorsiflexion rocks, hip flexor half-kneel stretch, thoracic rotations; 
  3) Activation: mini-band lateral walks, clamshells, glute bridge iso holds, terminal knee extensions (TKE) with band.
- Cooldown: easy cycle 5–8 min + quad/ham/glute/calf stretches 30–45 s + patellar tendon flushing (knee extensions no load, 15–20 reps) if comfortable.

Progression overview by phase
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): Foundation and tolerance. Isometrics, partial ROM, slow tempos, machine emphasis. Build quad tolerance without deep flexion; prioritize hip/glute strength and balance.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6): Strength accumulation. Increase load, introduce controlled bilateral squatting to box, split-stance patterns to tolerable depth, more unilateral hip work, and anti-rotation.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9): Strength and force control. Heavier sets in safe ROM, more frontal plane work (lateral patterns within ROM), eccentric control, sled work, and core integration for skiing.
- Phase 4 (Weeks 10–12): Peak strength and ski-specific preparation. Heavier loads in allowed ROM, longer isometric holds, deceleration drills without impact, transverse plane control, and endurance of posture for skiing.

Weekly structure template
- Day A: Lower emphasis (knee + hip) + core anti-rotation
- Day B: Upper emphasis + posterior chain/hip accessories
- Day C: Lower emphasis (hip hinge + unilateral) + core anti-lateral flexion
- Optional Day D (light): Mobility, cycling/row Z2 25–35 min, easy sled, balance

Load notation: RIR (reps in reserve). Rest 90–150 s for big lifts; 45–75 s accessories.

Here’s a simple, sustainable nutrition plan to maintain weight while supporting strength gains, joint health, and recovery across the 12-week program. Targets
- Calories: Maintenance. Start at bodyweight (kg) × 30–33 kcal/day. If weight changes >0.25%/week, adjust by 100–150 kcal/day.
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day (upper end on training days). Distribute over 3–5 feedings with 25–40 g high-quality protein each.

- Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day. Balance mono/polyunsaturated fats; include omega-3s.
- Fiber: 25–40 g/day from fruits, vegetables, legumes, and whole grains.
- Hydration: 30–40 ml/kg/day water. Add 500–750 ml during training; include electrolytes if sessions exceed 60 min or in heat.

Meal timing and training-day structure
- Pre-workout (1–2 h before): 
  - 0.5–1 g/kg carbs + 20–30 g protein; low fat/fiber for comfort.

- Post-workout (0–2 h after):

- Protein: Lean meats, eggs, dairy (Greek yogurt, cottage cheese), whey/plant protein, fish (salmon, trout, sardines 2–3×/week for omega-3s), tofu/tempeh.

- Fats: Olive oil, avocado, nuts/seeds, fatty fish. Limit deep-fried foods and excess omega-6 seed oils.

- Week 4
  - Day A: Leg press 4×8–10; Box squat 5×4; Spanish squat iso 3×30–45 s; Split squat to pads 3×6/side; calf 4×10–12; Pallof half-kneel 3×10/side.
  - Day B: Incline DB press 4×6–8; 1-arm cable row 4×8/side; landmine press 3×8/side; face pull 3×12–15; prone ham curl 3×8–10 (slow ecc); supported hip airplanes 3×4/side.
  - Day C: Trap bar DL 5×3; RDL 3×6–8; step-up 8–10 in 4×5/leg; Copenhagen plank (short lever) 3×15–20 s; suitcase carry 3×30–40 m/side.
- Week 5: +2.5–5% loads; add lateral sled drag 3×20 m/side (A or C); split squat slightly deeper only if zero next-day symptoms; shin vertical.
- Week 6: Box squat clusters 4×(2+2) w/20 s intra-rest; single-leg press 3×8/leg partial; reverse lunge to slightly lower box 3×6/leg; cable anti-rotation iso 3×20–30 s/side; add one 30–35 min Z2 ride this week if recovery is good.

Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9): Strength and force control
- Week 7
  - Day A: Box squat 5×3; Leg press 4×6–8; Spanish squat iso 3×40–50 s; Split squat 3×5/side (3–1–2 tempo); lateral band walks 3×12/side; Pallof step-outs 3×8/side.
  - Day B: Bench 5×3–5; chest-supported row 4×6–8; landmine press standing 3×6–8; single-leg RDL (assisted) 3×6/leg; Nordic curl assisted/ecc 3×3–5; prone Y-T-W 2×10.
  - Day C: Trap bar DL 5×2; RDL 3×5–6; step-up 10–12 in 4×4/leg; Copenhagen (medium) 3×20–25 s; suitcase carry 4×30–40 m/side.
- Week 8: Leg press 4×6 with 4 s eccentric; add shallow lateral step-downs 3×6/side if tolerable; SL RDL 3×7/leg; conditioning per cardio plan.
- Week 9: Box squat top singles to RPE ~7 (3 singles), then 3×3 @ 80%; Split squat 4×5/side slightly deeper if asymptomatic; add cable lift/chop 3×8/side; balance with head turns 3×20–30 s/side.

Phase 4 (Weeks 10–12): Peak strength and ski-specific control
- Week 10
  - Day A: Box squat 5×2 heavy (RIR 2); Leg press 3×5–6 (3 s ecc); Spanish squat 3×50–60 s; lateral sled drags 4×20 m/side; Pallof walkout 3×6 steps/side.
  - Day B: Incline DB press 4×5–6; 1-arm cable row 4×6–8 heavy; SL RDL 4×5/side; Nordic assisted 4×3; face pulls 3×12; back extension 3×10.
  - Day C: Trap bar DL 6×1–2 @ RPE 7–8; RDL 3×4–5; step-up 4×4/side heavier; Copenhagen 3×25–30 s; suitcase carry 4×40–50 m/side.
- Week 11: Box squat 3×2 slightly heavier (RIR 2); add split-squat isos mid-range 3×20–30 s/side; eccentric leg press (5 s down, 2 up/1 down) 3×4–5/leg; shallow lateral step-downs 3×5/side; intervals per cardio plan.
- Week 12 (deload/taper 30–40% volume, maintain intensity): 
  - Day A: Box squat 3×2 @ RPE 7; Leg press 2×5; Spanish squat 2×40–50 s; lateral band walks 2×10/side.
  - Day B: Bench 3×3; row 3×6–8; SL RDL 3×4/side; core lift/chop 2×8/side.
  - Day C: Trap bar 3×1–2 @ RPE 7–8; RDL 2×4; step-up 2×3/side; Copenhagen 2×20 s/side.

Cardio (2 sessions/week; low-impact; cadence > torque; knee pain ≤3/10)
- Weeks 1–3 (baseline)
  - S1: Z2 steady 30–35 min.
  - S2: 5×2 min Z3, 2 min easy (w/u and c/d each 8–10/5–8 min).
- Weeks 4–8 (increased volume/density)
  - Week 4: S1 3×10 min Z3 + 8 min Z2 (50–55 min). S2 4×8-min over/unders (52–55 min).
  - Week 5: S1 threshold ladders 2 rounds 4–5–6 min Z3 blocks (55–58 min). S2 SkiErg 6×2 min Z3 + Bike 20 min Z2 (50–55 min).
  - Week 6: S1 30 min Z2.5–Z3 with 30 s cadence surges every 5 min + 10 min Z2 (50–55 min). S2 over/under pyramids 3 rounds (55–58 min).
  - Week 7: S1 5×6 min “gates” 30 s Z3/30 s Z2 (55–60 min). S2 SkiErg 6×90 s Z3–low Z4 + Bike 25 min Z2–Z3 + 4×45 s pickups (50–55 min).
  - Week 8: S1 2×15 min Z3 + 10 min Z2 (55–60 min). S2 3×8 min Z3 + sled drags 6×20–25 m/side if knee calm (50–55 min).
- Peak Weeks 9–12
  - Week 9: S1 3×10 min Z3 + 8–10 min Z2 (50–55 min). S2 5×6 min gates 30/30 (50–55 min).
  - Week 10 (peak load): S1 threshold ladders (5–6–7 min Z3 blocks ×2; 55–60 min). S2 SkiErg 6×2 min Z3–low Z4 + Bike 25 min Z2–Z3 (50–55 min).
  - Week 11 (sharpen): S1 2×12 min Z3 + 6×30 s fast cadence (45–50 min). S2 2 rounds over/under pyramid (45–48 min).
  - Week 12 (taper): S1 2×8 min Z3 + 6–8 min Z2 (35–40 min). S2 3×5 min gates 20/40 + wall sits 2×45–60 s + optional skater isos 2×20 s/side (30–35 min).

Recovery and mobility
- Daily micro-routine (10–15 min): Foam roll quads/adductors/glutes/calves; ankle rocks 2×10/side; half-kneel hip flexor 2×30–45 s/side; 90/90 rotations 2×6–8/side; TKEs 2×15; glute bridge iso 2×20–30 s; mini-band walks 2×10/side; thoracic rotations 2×6/side; 2–3 min nasal breathing.
- Post-session cooldown (8–10 min): 5 min easy spin; stretch quads/hamstrings/calves/hip flexors/adductors 30–45 s; unweighted knee extensions 1–2×15–20 if comfortable.
- Two deeper sessions weekly (20–30 min)
  - Session A: Banded ankle mobs; elevated adductor rock backs; figure-4 stretch; hip flexor w/side-bend; supported hip airplanes 2×4–5/side; single-leg balance w/head turns.
  - Session B: Cat–camel; thread-the-needle; thoracic extension on roller; dead bugs; side planks; Pallof isos 2×20–30 s; wall sits 2×30–60 s at pain-free angle.
- Flare playbook: Reduce ROM 20–30%, swap knee-dominant work for hinges/isometrics, use compression/elevation; ice only if symptomatic; resume progress once next-day reactivity resolves.

Nutrition (maintenance bodyweight; support strength/recovery)
- Daily targets
  - Calories: Start BW(kg) × 30–33 kcal; adjust ±100–150 kcal if weekly average weight shifts >0.25%.
  - Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day, spread over 3–5 meals (25–40 g/meal).
  - Carbs: 3–4.5 g/kg/day; bias toward pre/post training.
  - Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day. Fiber 25–40 g/day. Hydration 30–40 ml/kg/day (+500–750 ml around training).
- Timing
  - Pre (1–2 h): 0.5–1 g/kg carbs + 20–30 g protein; low fat/fiber.
  - Post (0–2 h): 0.5–0.7 g/kg carbs + 25–40 g protein.
  - Rest days: keep protein; slightly reduce carbs (remove pre/post boluses).
- Food quality: lean proteins, dairy/eggs, fish 2–3×/wk; rice/potatoes/oats/fruit; olive oil/avocado/nuts; plenty of veg; vitamin C, calcium, vitamin D sources.
- Supplements (optional): Creatine 3–5 g/day; collagen/gelatin 10–15 g + 50–100 mg vitamin C 30–60 min pre-lower-body if tendon discomfort; omega-3 1–2 g EPA/DHA/day if low fish; whey/plant protein; magnesium glycinate 200–400 mg at night if needed.
- Tracking: Weigh 3–4 mornings/week; adjust intake to keep weight stable and performance high.

Return-to-ski readiness checks by Week 12
- Pain-free completion of sessions; no next-day swelling.
- Box squat and leg press strong in controlled ROM; trap bar singles at RPE 7–8 move crisply.
- Step-up to 10–12 in with control, no valgus; 60 s wall sit pain-free at training angle.
- Balance: 30 s single-leg with head turns/perturbations.
- Subjective confidence ≥8/10 on stairs, hills, and lateral moves.

Coach notes
- Progress one variable at a time (load, ROM, or density). Log box/step heights to progress safely.
- Keep cadence high/moderate resistance on cardio to avoid deep flexion.
- If knee reactivity appears, pull back cardio volume first, then lower-body ROM; keep upper body and hinge patterns rolling.
